subject: Comparing cell free dna from whole genome cellular dna on methylation-level basis

messages.author: 790e074c50910616
messages.subject: Comparing cell free dna from whole genome cellular dna on methylation-level basis
parts:
Hi,

Can someone suggest how can I compare methylation levels in cell-free DNA samples with methylation levels in whole-genome extracted DNA (i.e. from whole-cell)? My hypothesis is that both kinds of samples should have the same methylation levels but I need to know how to check that? I have three replicates sequenced from both kinds of methods. So far, I ran methylkit differential analysis on these 6 samples (taken 1 for cellular and 0 for cell-free extracted DNA samples) and got hypo and hyper methylation loci. However, this does not serve the purpose.
I would appreciate your suggestions.

Thanks,
Shruti

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Comparing cell free dna from whole genome cellular dna on methylation-level basis
parts:
The differentially methylated regions, in this case, depend on conversion efficiency, depth, and maybe other technical or biological variables I don't know about, all of which might create enough variation to call DMRs between cfDNA and whole-cell. I would cluster your samples with other WGBS data from different cell lines. If your expectations are correct, all your samples will cluster together away from other cell lines.

Best,
Altuna
